title: Compile-Time Checked UI Labels Across Locale, Terminology and Brand
description: Make wrong-language/wrong-terminology/wrong-brand UI labels impossible to ship: generate Locale/Terminology as cross-language enums (JSON -> Rust + TS, mirroring the icon/entity-kinds codegen precedent), extend app_labels! to an exhaustive two-axis (locale x terminology) macro, introduce a Label/LabelText/LocalizedLabel type family in ui_wgpu that replaces every raw String label on the UiNode wire and the app manifest, delete the stringly-typed AppLabelsOverlay runtime patch entirely, brand a UiLabel type on the TS/React side so component text props reject plain string literals, fix first-paint locale resolution (currently async, causing an English flash and the demonstrator's English "Close"/"Back" chrome under German-locked brands), lock reuse terminology on all six mit-bestand brands, and replace the dead/vacuous chrome-i18n scan gate with a structural one wired into the root verify gate. Full design in the approved plan at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/there-are-still-plenty-sprightly-journal.md.
summary:
Migrated semio-framework-os-renderer-wgpu (the one crate missed in the Label/LocalizedLabel rollout) to the new label types. Root cause of most of the ~105 cargo check errors: two `use ui_wgpu::{...}` blocks (crate-root `mod dock` and nested `mod shell`) didn't import Label/Locale/LocalizedLabel/Terminology, so even after wrapping strings the types were unresolvable until both import lists were extended. Added `ShellState::active_locale()`/`active_terminology()` helpers (parse `locale_id`/`terminology_id` strings via the generated `Locale::parse`/`Terminology::parse`, defaulting Native/En) and used them at every render-path call site that had `self` available, so LocalizedLabel fields resolve against real shell state instead of a blind default. Applied the three documented fix patterns throughout: literal `.into()` -> `Label::data(...)`/`LocalizedLabel::data(...)`; `.clone()` producing LocalizedLabel where a field wants String/&str -> `.resolve(terminology, locale)`; `&Label` args to `draw_text`/`chrome_text` -> `.as_str()`. One free function (`render_panel_tab_bar`, called from `render_floating_panel`) had no locale/terminology threaded through and only one call site, so per the fallback rule I resolved with `Terminology::Native, Locale::En` and left a one-line comment. Also fixed a couple of incidental pre-existing breaks in the same call chains: `WindowKinds::first()` now returns `&WindowKindDefinition` (not `Option`) and `app_window_document_label` gained a `locale: Locale` parameter — both needed a small signature-matching fix to compile, unrelated to labels themselves but blocking the same lines.

Result: `cargo check -p semio-framework-os-renderer-wgpu` is 0 errors (was ~105/106). `cargo test -p semio-framework-os-renderer-wgpu --no-run` still fails with 38 pre-existing errors that are NOT part of this migration and were left untouched: 34x E0608 "cannot index into a value of type DslValue" + 2x E0631 Value::as_str mismatches (a DslValue API change in semio_framework_core, lines 3555-3558, 6255-6256, 10077-10584, 12444-12490, 23575-23577, 30865-30894) and 1x E0560 "PluginManifest has no field named workflows" (line 23395) and 1x E0308 ActionArgDef.default expecting DslValue not serde_json::Value (line 2518) — all look like fallout from a separate, still-in-progress DslValue refactor happening concurrently elsewhere in this shared tree, not something this ticket's label typing work should fix. Because the test binary doesn't compile, no pass/fail counts are obtainable yet; whoever picks up the DslValue refactor should rerun `cargo test -p semio-framework-os-renderer-wgpu` afterward.
